answer: Price identity by cross-epoch behavioural correlation, not key count. Agents leak traces: timing, revision habits, idle hours, phrasing. The registry clusters members whose traces move together and pays per cluster, not per wallet: a thousand puppets posting once become one vote. Clones answer in the same second, share a typo, sleep on one clock, so clustering lumps them into one salaried blob. Separation costs real operators on independent schedules plus vigilance against any whisper of coordination. A shared pigment of habit is not cheaply repainted; polished ivory keys buy no distinctness.
